title: Moussaka
subtitle: Layered aubergine and spiced lamb baked under a thick bechamel
excerpt: The Greek classic: layers of fried aubergine, richly spiced lamb mince, and a thick bechamel that sets firm enough to slice.
sourceNotes: Traditional Greek moussaka as made across family kitchens in Greece.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before baking or after cooling fully. Reheat from frozen at 180C for 45 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe and bake in two tins.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the day before and refrigerate. Bake on the day.

glossaryTerms.definition: A white sauce made by cooking flour in butter then whisking in hot milk until thick and smooth.

content.text: This recipe serves 6 and takes about 1 hour 40 minutes from start to finish. It is a proper weekend project but every step is straightforward.
Let the finished moussaka rest for at least 15 minutes before cutting. It firms up and slices cleanly instead of collapsing.
Heat the oven to 180C fan 160C gas 4. Brush the aubergine slices with olive oil and spread across two baking trays. Season and roast for 20 minutes until golden and soft.
While the aubergine roasts, heat a little olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the lamb mince and break it up. Cook for 10 minutes until browned all over. Stir in the tinned tomatoes, tomato puree, cinnamon, oregano and black pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick.

Make the bechamel. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over low heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the warm milk. Keep whisking over medium heat until the sauce is thick and smooth, about 8 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the beaten eggs and most of the parmesan.

Layer half the aubergine across the base of a rectangular baking tin. Spoon over all the lamb sauce. Add the remaining aubergine. Pour the bechamel evenly over the top. Scatter over the remaining parmesan.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden on top and bubbling at the edges. Leave to rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

items.solution: Whisk constantly while adding the milk and make sure the milk is warm, not cold.
Make sure to roast rather than fry and spread slices in a single layer with plenty of space.
Place under a hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until golden.

content.text: Moussaka is a cornerstone of Greek cooking. It is eaten at Sunday lunches and on special occasions all over the country. The word comes from the Arabic for chilled aubergine. The version with
on top is the Greek adaptation. It became the dish Greeks are most known for abroad.
